long_biography.plain_text:
The Finkl family's industrial roots predated James by more than a century. Anton Finkl established the Chicago operation in 1879, and four generations developed it into a closely held producer of die steels, mould steels and custom forgings. James entered the company full time as the next generation, choosing personnel and product-sales responsibilities instead of the engineering route associated with his father and predecessors.

That distinction shaped his place in the succession. The firm relied on experienced professional management, while James gained commercial experience without becoming its principal technical operator. After Charles W. Finkl died, the family sold the operating business to settle his estate. James and two former executives retained the old mill property, preserving a direct interest in an industrial asset after steel production changed hands. The transition separated inherited ownership from day-to-day control and gave Finkl a platform for later activity beyond the family company.
